nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a bounds-valid range tree with at least one leaf. Then the cached lower bound of $t$ and the cached upper bound of $t$ are both leaf values of $t$.
nodes.title: The cached bounds of a nonempty bounds-valid range tree are leaf values

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a bounds-valid range tree, and write $t_{\min}$ and $t_{\max}$ for its cached lower and upper bounds. Then every leaf value $x$ of $t$ satisfies $t_{\min} \le x \le t_{\max}$.
nodes.title: Leaf values of a bounds-valid tree lie between the cached bounds

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of integers, the range tree built from $L$ by recursive halving is bounds-valid.
nodes.title: Built range trees are bounds-valid

nodes.summary: For a range tree $s$, write $s_{\min}$ and $s_{\max}$ for its cached lower and upper bounds: the stored interval endpoints at a node, the value itself at a leaf, and $0$ for the empty tree. Bounds-validity is defined inductively: the empty tree and every leaf are bounds-valid, and a node with cached interval $[a, b]$, left child $\ell$ and right child $r$ is bounds-valid when $\ell$ and $r$ are bounds-valid, each…
nodes.title: Bounds-valid range trees

nodes.summary: For a range tree $s$, write $s_{\min}$ and $s_{\max}$ for its cached lower and upper bounds. The range tree built from a list $L$ of integers of length $n$ is defined by recursion on $n$: the empty list gives the empty tree, a one-element list $[x]$ gives the leaf $x$, and for $n \ge 2$ it is the node whose left child $\ell$ is the tree built from the first $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ entries of $L$, whose right child…
nodes.title: Building a range tree from a list

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of integers and all integers $a$ and $b$, the range count over $[a, b]$ of the range tree built from $L$ equals the number of entries of $L$, counted with multiplicity, that lie in $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Range counting on a built tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a bounds-valid range tree and let $a$ and $b$ be integers. Then the range count of $t$ over $[a, b]$ equals the number of leaves of $t$ whose value lies in $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Range count of a bounds-valid tree

nodes.summary: For a range tree $t$ and integers $a$ and $b$, the range count of $t$ over $[a, b]$ is the length of the range report of $t$ for $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Range count

nodes.summary: For every range tree $t$, the list of leaf values of $t$ read from left to right has length equal to the number of leaves of $t$.
nodes.title: Length of the leaf list of a range tree

nodes.summary: For every list $L$ of integers and all integers $a$, $b$ and $x$, the value $x$ occurs in the range report for $[a, b]$ on the range tree built from $L$ if and only if $x$ is an entry of $L$ and $a \le x \le b$.
nodes.title: Range report membership on a built tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a range tree satisfying the bounds-correctness predicate: every node has two subtrees with at least one leaf each and caches the least and the greatest leaf value of its subtree. For all integers $a$, $b$ and $x$, the value $x$ occurs in the range report of $t$ for $[a, b]$ if and only if $x$ is a leaf value of $t$ and $a \le x \le b$.
nodes.title: Membership in a range report

nodes.summary: If a range tree $t$ is valid, then its list of leaf values, read from left to right, is sorted in nondecreasing order.
nodes.title: Valid range trees have sorted leaves

nodes.summary: A one-dimensional range tree over the integers is either empty, a single leaf holding an integer, or a binary node made of two integers $l$ and $h$ together with a left and a right subtree. The integers $l$ and $h$ are meant to cache the interval $[l, h]$ spanned by the leaf values of the node's subtree; the type does not enforce this, the bounds-correctness predicate does.
nodes.title: Range tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a bounds-valid range tree, let $a$ and $b$ be integers and let $\mathit{acc}$ be a list of integers. Then the accumulator range report of $t$ for $[a, b]$ starting from $\mathit{acc}$ is the list of the leaf values $x$ of $t$ with $a \le x \le b$, in left-to-right order and with repetitions, followed by $\mathit{acc}$.
nodes.title: Accumulator range report of a bounds-valid range tree

nodes.summary: For integers $a$, $b$ and a list $\mathit{acc}$ of integers, the accumulator range report of a range tree for $[a, b]$ starting from $\mathit{acc}$ is defined by recursion on the tree. The empty tree returns $\mathit{acc}$. A leaf with value $x$ returns $x$ followed by $\mathit{acc}$ if $a \le x \le b$, and $\mathit{acc}$ otherwise. A node with cached interval $[l, h]$ returns $\mathit{acc}$ if $h < a$ or $b < l$;…
nodes.title: Accumulator range report

nodes.summary: For every list $\mathit{xs}$ of integers and all integers $a$ and $b$, the range report for $[a, b]$ on the range tree built from $\mathit{xs}$ equals the list of elements $x$ of $\mathit{xs}$ with $a \le x \le b$, in their original order.
nodes.title: Range report on a built tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a range tree satisfying the bounds-correctness predicate: every node has two subtrees with at least one leaf each and caches the least and the greatest leaf value of its subtree. For all integers $a$ and $b$, the range report of $t$ for $[a, b]$ equals the list of leaf values $x$ of $t$ with $a \le x \le b$, in left-to-right order.
nodes.title: Correctness of the range report

nodes.summary: The range report of a range tree $t$ for integers $a$ and $b$ is the accumulator range report of $t$ for $[a, b]$ starting from the empty list.
nodes.title: Range report

nodes.summary: For every list $\mathit{xs}$ of integers, the range tree built from $\mathit{xs}$ has exactly as many leaves as $\mathit{xs}$ has elements.
nodes.title: Size of a built range tree

nodes.summary: The size of a range tree is its number of leaves: $0$ for the empty tree, $1$ for a leaf, and the sum of the sizes of the two children for a node.
nodes.title: Number of leaves of a range tree

nodes.summary: For a range tree $t$, $\operatorname{tmax}(t)$ is $0$ if $t$ is empty, $x$ if $t$ is a single leaf with value $x$, and the stored upper bound $hi$ if $t$ is a node with stored bounds $lo$, $hi$ and two subtrees.
nodes.title: Cached upper bound of a range tree

nodes.summary: For a range tree $t$, $\operatorname{tmin}(t)$ is $0$ if $t$ is empty, $x$ if $t$ is a single leaf with value $x$, and the stored lower bound $lo$ if $t$ is a node with stored bounds $lo$, $hi$ and two subtrees.
nodes.title: Cached lower bound of a range tree

nodes.summary: For every range tree $t$ and every list $a$ of integers, the accumulator leaf traversal of $t$ started from $a$ equals the leaf list of $t$ followed by $a$.
nodes.title: Range-tree leaf traversal appends to its accumulator

nodes.summary: For a range tree $t$ and a list $a$ of integers, $\operatorname{aux}(t, a)$ is $a$ if $t$ is empty, the list $x$ followed by $a$ if $t$ is a single leaf with value $x$, and $\operatorname{aux}(L, \operatorname{aux}(R, a))$ if $t$ is a node with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$.
nodes.title: Leaf traversal of a range tree with an accumulator

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of integers, the leaf list of the range tree built from $xs$ is $xs$.
nodes.title: Building a range tree preserves the list

nodes.summary: For all integers $lo$, $hi$ and range trees $L$, $R$, the leaf list of the node with stored bounds $lo$, $hi$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is the leaf list of $L$ followed by the leaf list of $R$.
nodes.title: Leaf list of a range-tree node

nodes.summary: The leaf list of a range tree $t$ is the list of the integers stored at its leaves, read from left to right and with repetitions.
nodes.title: Leaf list of a range tree

nodes.summary: For every list $xs$ of integers that is sorted in nondecreasing order, the range tree built from $xs$ is valid.
nodes.title: Building from a sorted list gives a valid range tree

nodes.summary: A range tree $t$ is valid when it has correct cached bounds (every node has two subtrees with nonempty leaf lists, and its stored lower and upper bounds are the minimum of the lower bounds and the maximum of the upper bounds of its two subtrees, recursively) and its leaf list is sorted in nondecreasing order.
nodes.title: Valid range tree

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
